resupply_point_count_source.section: chart, three 'Resupply Point' dots on the Guadalcanal northwest coast

resupply_rules.simultaneous_capacity_text: Each Resupply Point can only handle recovering three destroyer loads at one time.
resupply_rules.strings_per_ship_text: Each ship can carry five drum strings, but only one may be offloaded per turn.
resupply_rules.offload_rate: one drum string every Tactical Turn
resupply_rules.unloading_speed_text: During the unloading evolution, a destroyer's maximum speed is 2 knots - bare steerageway.
resupply_rules.undelivered_strings: Any drum strings that are not successfully offloaded will have their points deducted from the Japanese player's point total at the end of the scenario.
resupply_rules.damage_points: The Japanese player also receives one point for every damage point inflicted on a US ship.
resupply_rules.torpedo_reload_exception: Due to the weight of the drum strings, all Japanese destroyers with supplies cannot carry their torpedo reloads. Thus, only Naganami and Takanami have their full torpedo complement.

string_totals_derived.note: derived arithmetic (6 loaded ships x 5 strings x 20 points), not a printed total; the page prints the per-ship and per-string rules only

resupply_rules.string_duration: no per-string offload duration in minutes is printed; the rule is expressed in Tactical Turns only (see pending items)

orders.japan: The Reinforcement Unit is to offload supply drum strings at designated points off the coast of Guadalcanal. After unloading supplies, clear land-based aircraft range by dawn.

victory_conditions_as_printed.japanese_scoring: The Japanese player earns points for delivering supplies, as well as sinking or damaging US ships. However, any undelivered supply points will be deducted from the total at the end of the scenario.
victory_conditions_as_printed.us_decisive: Prevent the Japanese from delivering more than 120 supply points and with only one US heavy cruiser has being crippled (50% or more damage).
victory_conditions_as_printed.us_tactical: Prevent the Japanese from delivering more than 240 supply points and with only one US heavy cruiser being sunk).

japan.tier_label_adoption: the page prints both tiers as 'Decisive'; the RTS grading adopts 500 as Decisive and 250 as Tactical (see conflicts ijn-victory-tier-labels)

decisive.condition_scope: heavy cruisers only (Minneapolis, New Orleans, Pensacola, Northampton); Honolulu is a CL per the printed list

objective_reading_for_rts_fixture.testability: both the 500 and 250 Japanese thresholds and both the 120/240 US delivery thresholds are separately testable; the 500/250 conflict is resolved only at the RTS grading layer and the printed record above is retained verbatim
objective_reading_for_rts_fixture.user_visible_grading_note: player-facing tier names must state that the adopted grading is a RTS decision because the source prints two 'Decisive' tiers

conflicts.detail: Rising Sun PDF 75 (printed 74) prints 'Decisive: 500 or more total points.' followed by a second 'Decisive: 250 or more total points.' Both labels are retained verbatim in victory_conditions_as_printed. The RTS grading adopts 500/Decisive and 250/Tactical; player-visible content must mark this as an adopted grading, and both thresholds stay unit-testable.

US Decisive reads '...only one US heavy cruiser has being crippled (50% or more damage)' and Tactical ends with a stray ')'. Printed typos are retained; the reading registered is: at most one US CA at 50%+ damage (decisive), at most one US CA sunk (tactical).

American Fleets F-1 prints Mk15 TNT as one pair (87 DP, 45 kts / 6000 yd) and Torpex (99 DP) as 34/10000 and 27/15000 from 1943. cape-st-george-1943.json v2 registered us_mk15_tnt as 87 DP with all three pairs, citing the dated Form 10s. Whether the two low-speed pairs are available to TNT loads on 1942-11-30 is not resolved by either source here; the scenario-date row registered above is the F-1 TNT single pair.

A-19 remark 'Late 42: Center 5 inch gun replaced by 2 single 20mm' carries no exact date. The dated Form 10s for Drayton (Mar-May 42), Perkins (Jan-Feb 42) and Lamson (Dec-41) predate it. Gun fit on 1942-11-30 (5 x 5in/38 vs 4 x 5in/38 + 20mm) is not resolved; both printed alternatives are retained.

A-18 prints the Gridley main battery as 'F/A(1)4 Mk21, Mk24 5in/38'. The mount-sector expansion of this notation is not printed and was not interpreted; gun_mounts is left null for the Gridley profile.

The scenario text gives only 'seven destroyers in a tight column' with Takanami off Naganami's port bow (30 deg, 4000 yd) and Naganami bearing 283 deg at 11.9 nmi from Minneapolis. The chart lists the seven hulls (Suzukaze, Kawakaze, Kagero, Kuroshio, Oyashio, Makinami, Naganami) without per-ship seat marks. The Naganami-end-as-van reading registered in start.japan_formation is an interpretation from the picket position, not a printed order.

US orders name the van ('four US destroyers', lead 30 deg off Minneapolis's port bow at 4000 yd) and the trailing pair (off Northampton's port quarter, 2000 yd) without naming ships. The orders registered in start.us_formation follow the chart label listing (Fletcher, Perkins, Maury, Drayton; Minneapolis ... Northampton; Lamson, Lardner). Per-ship seats are not individually printed.
A-16 'Late 42: All were fitted with SC and SG search radar...' has no exact date; SC and Mk3 for Honolulu are confirmed by the Feb 42 remark. SG on Honolulu on 1942-11-30 is a candidate only.

A-19 '1942: Search radar fitted' does not name the type. Form 10 headers for Drayton/Perkins/Lamson were used only to confirm page mapping in this pass; the radar type stays unregistered beyond 'search radar (type not printed)'.

Scenario text confirms an SG contact on Minneapolis at 23:06. A-13 lists '2 Mk3, 2 SG, SK' only for the Nov 42 - Sep 43 repair period (post-battle). SC/Mk3 fit before the battle is not printed; only the SG is registered.
A-14 prints 'In Svc: 1929' for the Northampton class (US commissioned service 1930-31 in secondary references). The annex value is registered as printed and is not adjudicated here.

The Annex C rows above list every shell the scenario guns can fire (8in/55: APC, SpCOM, Com, HC; 6in/47: APC, HC; 5in/38 and 12.7cm/50 rows per the Cape package). Which shells each ship actually loads on 1942-11-30 is not printed in the verified sources; loadout selection stays with the runtime consumer.

Three 'Resupply Point' dots are printed on the chart (PDF 76 / printed 75) between Cape Esperance and Tassafaronga Point, but no coordinates are printed. Digitalization of the chart is a separate task; the 1.5 nmi radius rule cannot be exercised until the points are georeferenced.

The offload tempo is printed only as 'one drum string every Tactical Turn' / 'five turns to completely offload'; no wall-clock duration per string is printed. Runtime seconds-per-turn is an RTS adaptation and must not be back-filled into this record.

Form 10 index pages list Maury Dec-41 at 320 and 321, Kuroshio Dec-41 at 106 and 107, Oyashio Dec-41 at 109 and 110. Visual checks show printed page 321 = Bagley, 107 = Maikaze, 110 = Tanikaze; the working pages are Maury 320, Kuroshio 106, Oyashio 109. Kawakaze 127 and Suzukaze 137 are the 1943 configurations; the Dec-41 pages 128 and 138 are the ones applicable to this scenario.

A-25 ASW-refit remark dates: Kagero Apr-May 42 (before the scenario), Oyashio Jan-Mar 43 and Kuroshio Feb-Apr 43 (after). Kagero therefore carries the refit DC fit (2 rails w/6 DC + (2)2 Y-guns, 36 DC) and Oyashio/Kuroshio the base fit (6 racks w/1 DC, 18 DC + (2)1 Y-gun w/6 DC); both variants are registered.

Loaded destroyers: Makinami ('(Makinami carries supply drums)'), Transport Unit 1 (Oyashio, Kuroshio, Kagero) and Transport Unit 2 (Kawakaze, Suzukaze) - six hulls. Naganami and Takanami keep full torpedo reloads. The 'six barge/transport units' formulation in the roadmap note does not correspond to named units on the page; the only printed transport units are the two Desron 2 transport units of three and two destroyers.
